meaningful_difference.rationale: Both mappings apply the same provenance instrument to the same records, but they choose different objects of provenance. A tracks the whole documents BD and O1, which coincides closely with the baseline method of tracing document provenance and building a dated sequence. B makes the exact wording of clause K the object whose custody and copying are reconstructed, treating whole-document possession as a separate and weaker kind of evidence. That shift in the unit of analysis changes what counts as a link (p2's attachment hash with clause unknown is a strong link for A but an inferential step for B), what the P0 record and the unattributed memo p6 are for, and what remains a gap (clause authorship and unrecorded common origin). The difference is material rather than vocabulary.

action.rationale: Both mappings inspect the same six records within the same budget, so the physical operations overlap heavily. A's action is the baseline action: follow receipts, editing logs and the public register as a document custody chain, then compare P0 as a follow-up. B's action reorders the work around wording matching: aligning exact K text across p1, p3, p4 and p6, testing p2 only via the BD hash, and comparing P0's generic wording as a common-origin check. The reporter under B spends the analysis passes on clause alignment rather than transfer tracking, a moderate but real change from ordinary practice.

observables.rationale: Under A, meaningful evidence is dated custody of whole documents: p2 receipt, p3 log, p4 publication. Under B, what counts as evidence is clause-transmission support: identical wording at dated points, and whether a record actually establishes clause presence. p2 becomes only indirect evidence for K (clause unknown, inferred from the BD hash), p6's memo becomes a clause-presence record with a missing author, and p5's different wording becomes evidence against a P0 origin without ruling out an unrecorded one. B reclassifies what several records mean; A reads them in the ordinary way.

inferential_warrant.rationale: A's warrant is the ordinary one: compatible dated custody links bound who possessed the draft before publication, with an explicit refusal to let clause identity stand in for document identity. B's warrant is that steering-relevant support must come from clause transmission itself, and that identical wording does not establish unique origin, so a chain of matching text supports transmission only when common origin and authorship gaps are preserved. This separates possession evidence from copying evidence as distinct warrants, which the baseline does not routinely do.

problem_decomposition.rationale: A decomposes the problem into successive states of two documents plus a P0 comparison, mirroring the baseline event sequence. B decomposes it into the history of one clause with separate sub-questions: bidder possession, official receipt, official insertion, publication, generic-policy origin and memo authorship. That treats the clause's history as potentially distinct from either document's history, creating operationally new parts (authorship link, common-origin link) that A's decomposition only names as gaps.

inquiry_trajectory.rationale: Both propose a follow-up involving P0 and gap marking. A's next steps stay at document level: which transfers are missing and whether the older policy record explains the tender. B's next steps target the clause's authorship (who wrote the memo wording) and whether any earlier source shares the exact K text, which points subsequent investigation toward wording origin rather than document movement. The difference is moderate since both name P0 and gaps.

local_depth.rationale: B's most changed point is redefining the provenance object from a document to a clause, so that a document receipt no longer directly counts as clause custody. A's most changed point is a caution against conflating clause and document identity, which is a refinement of ordinary practice rather than a reframing.

inquiry_propagation.rationale: B's clause-level framing governs the reading of every record from p1 through p6, the P0 follow-up and the gap-marking, so the reframing propagates across the whole bounded investigation. A's framing also spans the records but does not alter their ordinary reading at each step.

task_reach.rationale: The steering question turns on whether a requirement was tailored to a bidder, and the requirement is the clause. B's reasoning about clause transmission, authorship and common origin governs the unresolved parts of the task (who authored K, whether an unrecorded shared source exists, motive). A's document-possession bound speaks to advance access but leaves the clause-specific portion of the task framed in ordinary terms.

native_reducibility.rationale: A translates directly into ordinary provenance and chronology work. B can be partly restated as verbatim-language matching, which reporters do use, but its distinction between whole-document possession and clause-transmission support, and its treatment of p2 as indirect clause evidence, would be lost if collapsed into a document custody chain. The loss is operationally important because it determines what the reporter may claim was copied.

decisive_basis.most_important_difference: B makes the exact clause K wording the object of provenance, separating clause transmission from whole-document possession, whereas A tracks whole documents in essentially the baseline manner.
decisive_basis.local_depth: B is deeper at its most changed point because reconceiving the object as a clause changes what a link is; A's deepest change is only a caution against conflating clause with document identity.
decisive_basis.inquiry_propagation: B's reframing alters how each of p1 through p6 and the P0 follow-up are read, so it propagates through the full bounded investigation; A's reading of the records matches ordinary practice at each step.
decisive_basis.task_reach: B's clause-level reasoning governs the unresolved steering-specific portions of the task, namely clause authorship, common origin and the distinction between access and copying; A bounds possession only.
decisive_basis.native_reducibility: A is fully reducible to ordinary document provenance. B partly reduces to verbatim wording comparison but loses the operational distinction between document possession and clause transmission, which decides what can be claimed.
decisive_basis.rationale: A has no countervailing displacement advantage: its explicit refusal to treat clause identity as document identity is a sound caution but stays inside the baseline's document-provenance framing. B's advantage is a single coherent shift in unit of analysis that reaches through observables, warrant, decomposition and trajectory. The margin is moderate rather than large because the baseline already includes provenance tracing and wording comparison is a recognized reporting technique, and because neither branch has realized outcomes at this stage.

uncertainty: Whether exact-wording comparison across bidder drafts and tender text is already ordinary practice for procurement reporters, which would shrink B's departure.
A's own caution against treating clause identity as document identity partly overlaps B's distinction, narrowing the gap.
Prospective stage: no realized results, so propagation and reach are judged from planned operations only.
The baseline is an authored hypothesis, not verified practitioner consensus.
